readings.title: The Revolt Against Abimelek
readings.subtitle: Gaal Challenges the King
readings.text: [Judges 9:22] And Abimelek reigned over Israel three years. [23] And <dn>Elohim</dn> sent an evil spirit between Abimelek and the men of Sheḵem, and the men of Sheḵem acted treacherously against Abimelek, [24] to bring the violence done to the seventy sons of Yerubbaʽal, and their blood, to be laid upon Abimelek their brother, who killed them, and upon the men of Sheḵem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers. [25] And the men of Sheḵem set men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them along that way. And it was reported to Abimelek. [26] And Gaʽal son of Eḇeḏ came with his brothers and went over to Sheḵem. And the men of Sheḵem put their trust in him. [27] And they went out into the fields, and gathered grapes from their vineyards and trod them, and held a festival, and went into the house of their mighty one, and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelek. [28] And Gaʽal son of Eḇeḏ said, “Who is Abimelek, and who is Sheḵem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Yerubbaʽal, and is not Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem. But why should we serve him? [29] “If only this people were under my hand! Then I would remove Abimelek.” And he said to Abimelek, “Increase your army and come out!” [30] And when Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaʽal son of Eḇeḏ, his displeasure burned. [31] And he sent messengers to Abimelek secretly, saying, “See, Gaʽal son of Eḇeḏ and his brothers have come to Sheḵem. And see, they are besieging the city against you. [32] “And now, rise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field. [33] “And it shall be, as soon as the sun is up in the morning, that you rise early and rush upon the city. And see, when he and the people who are with him come out against you, you shall do to them as your hand finds to do.” [34] So Abimelek rose by night, and all the people who were with him, and they lay in wait against Sheḵem in four companies. [35] And Gaʽal son of Eḇeḏ went out and stood in the entrance to the city gate. And Abimelek and the people who were with him rose from lying in wait. [36] And Gaʽal saw the people, and said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!” But Zebul said to him, “You see the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.” [37] And Gaʽal spoke again and said, “See, people are coming down from the center of the land, and another company is coming from the Diviners’ Terebinth Tree.” [38] Then Zebul said to him, “Where is your mouth now, with which you said, ‘Who is Abimelek, that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people whom you despised? Go out, please, and fight with them.” [39] And Gaʽal went out before the men of Sheḵem and fought against Abimelek. [40] And Abimelek pursued him, and he fled from him. And many fell wounded, up to the entrance of the gate. [41] And Abimelek dwelt at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaʽal and his brothers from dwelling in Sheḵem.

readings.title: The Judgment of Abimelek
readings.subtitle: Jotham's Curse Fulfilled
readings.text: [42] And it came to be on the next day that the people went out into the field, and they reported it to Abimelek. [43] And he took his people, and divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the field, and looked and saw the people, coming out of the city. And he rose against them and smote them. [44] And Abimelek and the company that was with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and the other two companies rushed upon all who were in the fields and smote them. [45] And Abimelek fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people who were in it, and he broke down the city and sowed it with salt. [46] And when all the men of the tower of Sheḵem heard that, they entered the stronghold of the house of the mighty one Berith. [47] And it was reported to Abimelek that all the men of the tower of Sheḵem had gathered together. [48] And Abimelek went up to Mount Tsalmon, he and all the people who were with him. And Abimelek took an axe in his hand and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it and laid it on his shoulder. And he said to the people who were with him, “What you have seen me do, make haste and do as I have done.” [49] And each of the people also cut down his own bough and followed Abimelek, and put them against the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire above them, so that all the people of the tower of Sheḵem died, about a thousand men and women. [50] And Abimelek went to Těḇěts, and encamped against Těḇěts and captured it. [51] But there was a strong tower in the city, and all the men and women and all the people of the city fled there and shut themselves in, and went up to the top of the tower. [52] And Abimelek came as far as the tower and fought against it, and drew near the door of the tower to burn it with fire. [53] And a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone on Abimelek’s head, and broke his skull. [54] And he quickly called the young man, his armour-bearer, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” So his young man thrust him through, and he died. [55] And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelek was dead, they went every man to his place. [56] Thus <dn>Elohim</dn> repaid the evil of Abimelek, which he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers. [57] And all the evil of the men of Sheḵem <dn>Elohim</dn> brought back on their own heads, and on them came the curse of Jotham son of Yerubbaʽal.

readings.title: The Minor Judges
readings.subtitle: Tola and Yair
readings.text: [Judges 10:1] And after Abimelek there arose to save Israel Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Yissasḵar, and he dwelt in Shamir in the mountains of Ephraim. [2] And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir. [3] And after him arose Ya’ir, a Gilʽaḏite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years. [4] And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities, which are called Ḥawwoth Ya’ir to this day, which are in the land of Gilʽaḏ. [5] And Ya’ir died and was buried in Qamon.

readings.title: Israel's Idolatry and Misery
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Soul is Shortened
readings.text: [6] And the children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and served the Baʽals and the Ashtaroth, and the mighty ones of Aram, and the mighty ones of Tsiḏon, and the mighty ones of Mo’aḇ, and the mighty ones of the children of Ammon, and the mighty ones of the Philistines. And they forsook <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and did not serve <dn>Him</dn>. [7] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Israel, and <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon. [8] And they crushed and oppressed the children of Israel that year – for eighteen years, all the children of Israel who were beyond the Yarden in the land of the Amorites, in Gilʽaḏ. [9] And the children of Ammon passed over the Yarden to fight against Yehuḏah, and against Binyamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was sorely distressed. [10] And the children of Israel cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “We have sinned against <dn>You</dn>, because we have both forsaken our <dn>Elohim</dn> and served the Baʽals!” [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to the children of Israel, <dq>“Did <dn>I</dn> not save you from the Mitsrites, and from the Amorites, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?</dq> [12] <dq>“And when the Tsiḏonians and Amalěq and Maʽon oppressed you, you cried out to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> saved you from their hand.</dq> [13] <dq>“But you have forsaken <dn>Me</dn> and served other mighty ones. Therefore <dn>I</dn> do not save you again.</dq> [14] <dq>“Go and cry out to the mighty ones which you have chosen, let them save you in the time of your distress.”</dq> [15] And the children of Israel said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “We have sinned! Do to us whatever is good in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, only deliver us this day, please.” [16] And they put away the foreign mighty ones from among them and served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>His</dn> being could no longer bear the misery of Israel. [17] And the children of Ammon were called together and encamped in Gilʽaḏ. And the children of Israel assembled together and encamped in Mitspah. [18] And the people, the heads of Gilʽaḏ, said to each other, “Who is the man who begins to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilʽaḏ.”

readings.title: Jephthah the Outcast
readings.subtitle: Called to Deliver Gilead
readings.text: [Judges 11:1] Now Yiphtaḥ the Gilʽaḏite was a mighty man of valour, but he was the son of a whore. And Gilʽaḏ brought forth Yiphtaḥ. [2] And the wife of Gilʽaḏ bore sons. And when his wife’s sons grew up, they drove Yiphtaḥ out, and said to him, “You do not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.” [3] And Yiphtaḥ fled from his brothers and dwelt in the land of Toḇ. And worthless men gathered to Yiphtaḥ and went out with him. [4] And it came to be, after some time, that the children of Ammon fought against Israel. [5] And it came to be, when the children of Ammon fought against Israel, that the elders of Gilʽaḏ went to get Yiphtaḥ from the land of Toḇ. [6] And they said to Yiphtaḥ, “Come and be our commander, and let us fight against the children of Ammon.” [7] But Yiphtaḥ said to the elders of Gilʽaḏ, “Did you not hate me, and expel me from my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?” [8] And the elders of Gilʽaḏ said to Yiphtaḥ, “That is why we have turned again to you now, that you may go with us and fight against the children of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilʽaḏ.” [9] And Yiphtaḥ said to the elders of Gilʽaḏ, “If you take me back home to fight against the children of Ammon, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives them to me, shall I be your head?” [10] And the elders of Gilʽaḏ said to Yiphtaḥ, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is witness between us, if we do not do according to your words.” [11] Then Yiphtaḥ went with the elders of Gilʽaḏ, and the people made him head and commander over them. And Yiphtaḥ spoke all his words before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Mitspah.

readings.title: The Dispute with Ammon
readings.subtitle: Jephthah's Legal Defense
readings.text: [12] And Yiphtaḥ sent messengers to the sovereign of the children of Ammon, saying, “What have you to do with me, that you have come against me to fight in my land?” [13] And the sovereign of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Yiphtaḥ, “Because Israel took away my land when they came up out of Mitsrayim, from the Arnon as far as the Yabboq, and to the Yarden. And now, give them back in peace.” [14] And Yiphtaḥ again sent messengers to the sovereign of the children of Ammon, [15] and said to him, “Thus said Yiphtaḥ, ‘Israel did not take away the land of Mo’aḇ, nor the land of the children of Ammon, [16] for when they came up from Mitsrayim, Israel walked through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Qaḏesh. [17] ‘And Israel sent messengers to the sovereign of Edom, saying, “Please let me pass through your land.” But the sovereign of Edom did not listen. And he also sent to the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, but he would not. So Israel stayed in Qaḏesh. [18] ‘Then he went through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Mo’aḇ, and came to the east side of the land of Mo’aḇ, and encamped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the border of Mo’aḇ, for the Arnon was the border of Mo’aḇ. [19] ‘And Israel sent messengers to Sihon sovereign of the Amorites, sovereign of Ḥeshbon. And Israel said to him, “Please let us pass through your land into our place.” [20] ‘But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his border, so Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Yahats, and fought against Israel. [21] ‘And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them. Thus Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that land. [22] ‘And they took possession of all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Yabboq and from the wilderness to the Yarden. [23] ‘And now <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel has driven out the Amorites from before <dn>His</dn> people Israel, should you then possess it? [24] ‘Do you not possess whatever Kemosh your mighty one has caused you to possess? So we possess all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> has driven out from before us. [25] ‘And now, are you any better than Balaq son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ? Did he ever strive against Israel? Did he ever fight against them? [26] ‘While Israel dwelt in Ḥeshbon and its villages, and in Aroʽer and its villages, and in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon, for three hundred years, why did you not recover them within that time? [27] ‘So I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me evil by fighting against me. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the Judge judge today between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.’ ” [28] However, the sovereign of the children of Ammon did not listen to the words which Yiphtaḥ sent him.
